The first Test's lineups paired Harry Wilson's Wallabies against Codie Taylor's All Blacks; Sydney selection is still to come. Taylor's captaincy covers Ardie Savea's shoulder-surgery absence, while Scott Barrett's return adds experience to New Zealand's pack. Both coaches now have direct evidence from Auckland rather than just South African form to assess. The question for this week is which combinations can sustain their work when territory and fatigue begin to change the game.

Australia and New Zealand meet at Accor Stadium on Saturday 17 October, a week after their Eden Park Test. This closes the Wallabies' home programme before their northern tour. The immediate contest is over territory, sustained pressure and the bench's ability to keep combinations working late in the match. The 2027 World Cup reunion here is confirmed for 9 October; this year's Sydney starting XV is not assumed. No prior-match outcome or future result is revealed in this preview.

For Australian supporters, the last home Test of the year is a chance to see Les Kiss's project hold its shape against the closest rival, not merely to applaud promising passages. Dave Rennie knows the gold jersey from his own time coaching Australia; facing his former players adds a personal edge to New Zealand's preparation. The crowd can supply belief, but it cannot make the tackles or organise the next phase. This stadium hosts the countries' first World Cup pool meeting next year, so the emotional memory of Sydney will outlast this fortnight.

Australia's preparation now points towards Munster at five-eighth, with Moses reported as the leading halfback contender; those reports are not a final team sheet. Yeo has confirmed he is deferring pectoral surgery to captain the squad. New Zealand bring Hughes back after an injury-enforced international absence, with Fisher-Harris leading a squad that adds Ponga and Gagai. The opening contest must turn those assembled strengths into a working spine and forward platform.

Thursday's Allianz Stadium opener begins Pool A, alongside Fiji and Cook Islands. Its points shape the route through the group; they do not award the trophy. Australia need a new attacking combination to function under pressure, while New Zealand's forwards must give their playmakers room to choose rather than merely react. Confirmed squad membership is separate from an announced match-day role. Australian coverage is on Seven and 7plus, and no recent match outcome is disclosed in this preview.

Hughes says his World Cup ambition reaches beyond the dressing room: he remembers what New Zealand's 2008 title meant to him as a child and wants today's young supporters to feel that connection. Yeo's decision carries a different cost, postponing surgery with his club's support. Munster faces a teammate whose decisions he knows from training, but familiarity works both ways. For both countries, belonging is now a responsibility to build something together, not just a jersey to wear.
